facts.heading: Anxiety started in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time, and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was the deputy head at her school.
facts.evidence: I was my deputy head at my school

facts.heading: Taught for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for for 11 years

facts.heading: Worries about competence
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking people will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person. And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Rehearses in mind nightly
facts.content: Hannah rehearses what she might say for meetings on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearses potential criticism
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say.
facts.evidence: I rehearse every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Imagines being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines that people think she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth, that they gave the job to a nice year four teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr. Hargraves is kind
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind.

facts.heading: Feels like she is lying
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capability.
facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted. That makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feels like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a head teacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a head teacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a head teacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother was brilliant
facts.content: Hannah's mother was brilliant, and people still praise her.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me saying what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Comparing self to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what her mother might have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's support is surface
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface.
facts.evidence: She's very supportive on the surface.

facts.heading: Mother's comment about worry
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hides the extent of worry
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad her anxiety is.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning. She falls asleep fine.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine.

facts.heading: Waking through to-do list
facts.content: Hannah goes through a to-do list when she is awake at four AM. The list includes various concerns.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah has been drinking a lot of coffee to get through the day since the second week of term. She knows this does not help.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Drinking five or six cups
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee. This leads to physical symptoms in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: Five or six.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: During the afternoons, Hannah notices her heart speeds up and her hands shake.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water due to physical symptoms. She does not think anyone noticed.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Feeling exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day because of pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben suggested she should just enjoy her situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Guilt and feeling alone
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives this advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's profession
facts.content: Ben is an engineer. He thinks something is a problem if it is said.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer. He thinks something's a problem if it's said.

facts.heading: Difficulty fixing problems
facts.content: Hannah expresses a wish that the situation were simple. She does not wish it were that simple.
facts.evidence: No, I wish it were that simple.

facts.heading: Lack of friends at school
facts.content: Hannah does not have friends at school who can talk to her anymore.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4 corridor with the others.

facts.heading: Current role as line manager
facts.content: Hannah is now the line manager and metal-crate. This role came with a company promotion.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and metal-crate.

facts.heading: Missing class and promotion
facts.content: Hannah missed her class and thought she did not want the promotion. She said yes because she could not say no to her.
facts.evidence: I missed my class too. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her

facts.heading: Crying after promotion decision
facts.content: Hannah went home and cried after accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried

facts.heading: Regret about not returning
facts.content: Hannah thought she would never get to go back. She questioned if she would want to go back.
facts.evidence: That I would never get to go back. Would you want to go back?

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays. They went walking in the lakes and did not think about school for ten days.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Difference during holiday
facts.content: During the holiday, nobody expected anything of her. She was just talking, and Ben carried the sandwiches.
facts.evidence: Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking. Ben carried the sandwiches.

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: The week before a term started, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before a term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things, a chill laugh thing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Stopped writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing down good things because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well was not the same as bragging.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal for meeting behavior
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing or sending emails.
facts.evidence: Mmm, walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first, sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for evening relaxation
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings about goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and lighter when discussing her goals.
facts.evidence: Lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: First time sharing bad news
facts.content: Hannah has told someone how bad things are for the first time.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah is scared about telling Ben how bad things are.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Choosing time to share news
facts.content: Hannah plans to try telling Ben this week if she chooses a quiet moment.
facts.evidence: Nooooooo, I might try this week.

facts.heading: Preferred time to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah prefers Saturday morning over a Sunday evening to tell Ben.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too warmed up. Saturday morning, perhaps? He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Trying notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for one week.
facts.evidence: Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line. I could.
